Content covers: Rabbi Yehuda's view that the indispensable decree (chukkah) applies to a place whose atonement occurs only once a year (the Holy of Holies) but not to the Sanctuary/courtyards more broadly; the derivation from the doubled words 'zot' and 'achat' excluding the outer white-garment and golden-garment acts from that decree; the parallel dispute over whether pouring the remainder of the blood is itself indispensable, tied to whether the other white-garment acts are indispensable; Rabbi Akiva's and Rabbi Yehuda's competing readings of 'vechillah mechaper et hakodesh' as to whether completing the essential sprinklings alone completes atonement; and the challenge from Rabbi Yochanan's own ruling in Zevachim (that offering the remainder outside the Temple incurs the karet penalty for outside offerings) showing that the remainder must itself be an indispensable inside service, which the Gemara starts to reconcile with the Mishnah's own ruling about bringing new blood when the first bull's blood is spilled mid-service.
